title: Health Education Specialists
description: Provide and manage health education programs that help individuals, families, and their communities maximize and maintain healthy lifestyles. Use data to identify community needs prior to planning, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating programs designed to encourage healthy lifestyles, policies, and environments. May link health systems, health providers, insurers, and patients to address individual and population health needs. May serve as resource to assist individuals, other health professionals, or the community, and may administer fiscal resources for health education programs.

tasks.text: Develop and present health education and promotion programs, such as training workshops, conferences, and school or community presentations.
Develop educational materials and programs for community agencies, local government, and state government.
Develop operational plans and policies necessary to achieve health education objectives and services.
Design and administer training programs for new employees and continuing education for existing employees.
Maintain databases, mailing lists, telephone networks, and other information to facilitate the functioning of health education programs.
Document activities and record information, such as the numbers of applications completed, presentations conducted, and persons assisted.
Develop, prepare, and coordinate grant applications and grant-related activities to obtain funding for health education programs and related work.
Prepare and distribute health education materials, such as reports, bulletins, and visual aids, to address smoking, vaccines, and other public health concerns.
Develop and maintain health education libraries to provide resources for staff and community agencies.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Collaborate with health specialists and civic groups to determine community health needs and the availability of services and to develop goals for meeting needs.
Design and conduct evaluations and diagnostic studies to assess the quality and performance of health education programs.
Develop and maintain cooperative working relationships with agencies and organizations interested in public health care.
Develop, conduct, or coordinate health needs assessments and other public health surveys.
Supervise professional and technical staff in implementing health programs, objectives, and goals.
Provide program information to the public by preparing and presenting press releases, conducting media campaigns, or maintaining program-related Web sites.
Provide guidance to agencies and organizations on assessment of health education needs and on development and delivery of health education programs.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Mentimeter, Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Blackboard software, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention CDC WONDER, Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Blogging software, Facebook, Wiki software.
